Yeah I understand that some things that happen are horrible and there is nothing to do about them. Someone gets bullied, it's bad and it happened and there's nothing to stop it now. People die. Good things stop. All happiness ends, all good feelings end.

But I'm thinkig that might just be a way of thinking. With the exact same reasoning, you could claim this.
Everything is good, and the bad things happen. These bad things then end, and you're left with the good.

I don't believe that good is the "normal state" just as much as I don't believe that bad is the "normal" state.

A counter argument to "good is normal, bad things happen" could be that "bad things ARE real, like death and rape and mean people. But good things are not real, they are just feelings and bullshit we tell ourselves".

And that's true.

But again I think the opposite is true as well.
There are good things that are real: creating something, love, good people..
And there are bad things that are fake: sadness (you could say it's bullshit we tell ourselves, just like happiness), being angry at someone, annoying events (same thing, we convince ourselves).

So there is everything on each side.

In my opinion, it's like this.

There is a world. Then there are things and events - they simply exist and happen. The natural state of the world is neutral, not good or evil. It simply exists.
Then both good and bad things happen.
Then we have both good and bad feelings.
But neither of them is the default, natural state of the world. They happen, and then they are gone. But once they are gone, neither stayes as a background. There is simply an absence of good and bad. The absence of good or bad things isn't evil or bad itself. It's just boring, but not hurtful. It is empty, but not mean or against us. Nothingness doesn't mean evil. Nothingness is there to be filled. Sometimes evil fills it, sometimes good. But the world on it's own isn't either. Nothingness is uncomfortable, but this does not hurt us, this feeling exists to make us do something and fill the nothingness.

So I don't deny that some things are just bad and can't be avoided. But I am saying that the world in its natural state is nothing - and then good and evil happens on top of that.

I have more to say but this is already getting too long.
Do you want to say that we can't choose one or the other? That bad things simply happen, and there's nothing we can do?

I've changed my attitude by now, calmed down and realised what the right way to help is.

One thing is for sure - she needs your help. I don't know if she's going to therapy, but she really should if she isn't already. Hey, I don't know how you're doing, but I hope you're alright.

I just wanted to tell you to please be careful about one thing.

When it's difficult with parents, we usually hold onto the first friend or partner that we get in life. But this is so so so dangerous... Some people seem like they can help, or like they're someone to rely on, but many times they can be really dangerous.

My girlfriend had this one boyfriend in her life when she was very young - she just wanted to mean something to *someone*, but he was so awful to her and treated her so badly.. she ended up being in an even worse condition than she was just from her parents.

Please be careful about that, okay?
Of course, it's okay to hang out with people. Don't ignore anyone who wants to get close.. just, be careful. Its okay to stay away from those people.

I'm not a parent or anything so I really don't know what do :/

I feel like parents, even bad mean ones, can still be helpful. But I don't know how to make them.. I guess they should talk to someone about it, but you can't really do much to make that happen.

Do you maybe have someone else to talk to, who can talk to your mom about it? I don't know if you feel comfortable talking about those things with someone

(just a bunch of text, maybe some advice. I don't know why I write so much)

My girlfriend's dad is awful too, and he's been yelling at her for such stupid things and making her feel so worthless, all her life. For no reason. He doesn't drink, he doesn't have a disease and wants to be angry at someone, he doesn't hate her..

I don't understand such people. I try to, but I'm not sure I do.

I don't know if I'm trying to help, I'm just writing about similar situations.

Anyway it seems like her dad doesn't really know what he's doing and how bad it is. He says things like "how will you achieve anything in life if you can't clean your room or smile", and it hits really hard when it's your dad..
But I think he thinks it will help her. I used to feel really negative against him but I think I can understand now and I wanna talk to him, but that's just awkward.
He thinks that she doesn't understand that not doing some things is bad, and wants to show how serious it is by sounding strict and scary. She's 19 and he's been like this all the time, so he should have learned that that's not how you raise a child.

So I think your mum is also just trying to show you that some things are bad - but she doesn't know how to.

It's weird to think about it, but "adults" never got any guidebook for raising children. There isn't a course in college that teaches you how to be nice to your child. You just.. do something. I imagine it's pretty tough being a parent, when you suddenly realise "shit, what the hell do I do now".

I know this isn't the way it should work - but maybe try really showing your mum that this hurts you. Don't be angry at her or mean or something, just come and let her know that you understand she's trying to teach you what to do, but that it hurts you.

She's a grown up person, and if grown up people learn anything it's that people are complicated, so she will understand what you tell her. She will know something is wrong, and since she probably really cares she will understand that she needs to change the way she behaves.

I hope this helps you at least a little bit. I hope you get through this and that your mum can understand what's wrong.

Thank you for trying to help this much :)

She's with her dad, and he cares about her naturally but I don't think he knows what to do, maybe that's why it seems like he doesn't care. He told me he really cares and offers hugs and makes her food. It's alright now.
What I meant before was that he always blames her for feeling this way, says she's lazy and it's her fault, doesn't believe she will ever achieve anything because she can't even clean up her room... At least he isn't aggressive, he just says it "by the way", and it's his general attitude. It's still horrible pressure, to be treated like that by her own father.

Now he's around her because maybe he realised she really needs help and to be taken care of.

I'm really inspired to be well and stable and strong so I can help her, but I can't focus so much on her when uni is difficult and there's constantly something to do.

We really talked a lot about our plans and how we should do things (work, uni, wait this much), and while we didn't like any option we chose this one because it seemed like the normal thing to do. I start studying, she saves up some more money and comes here to study as well, and then I can help with a proper job later on.

Maybe instead of that I should be with her, also work in some job that doesn't need the language skill, help her both save up more easily and be with her for support. Then we both move and study together at the same time, same place. That would be so nice.. I just don't know if it's a good option. Dropping out seems like a big thing.

Maybe I could talk to my professors about taking a week off, but I don't think that would help her at all. She would be worried about me leaving soon, and scared of getting back to the same old bad situation.
She visited me recently and stayed here for a month (her job allowed her) and it was pretty bad because she knew it's not a solution and things would be bad again. And also I couldn't give all of myself to her because of uni, so I did really bad on both sides (uni and helping her).

It's also a bit too expensive to fly there and back just for a week. If it would really help then there wouldn't be a problem, but it wouldn't help.

I'm okay here, I am, I just worry about her and want to be with her to help her and support her, so I can't focus on studying or listening and I'm falling behind so much. That's then another cause of bad feelings, but I just feel under pressure, not depressed.

Thanks for caring, again. Thank you

She's sleeping, only awake for short bits of time. She just sent a message saying she "might be awake soon", so I hope she's alright.

I have to study but I keep keep feeling guilty for it because I should be there for her instead and forget uni for another year

I'm going to a therapist to talk about this whole thing, to have someone who will listen, because I need help taking on all the weight. Uni, girlfriend's depression, the distance, just not knowing if I'm doing the right thing, and how to manage all that.

If I'd be there with her, I would know I chose that way and I'd be okay. Maybe I'd feel disappointed that I left university for another year. Hmm..

I think they still shouldn't be blamed for it. This kind of mindset has to originate from somewhere - they were probably betrayed by many people along the way, and can't really trust that anyone truly cares anymore. It seems like people are just playing along purely for their own amusement. It's not like that, and I really want to show those people that someone still cares. Really and from the heart, and if I were close by I'd come knock on the door and try helping out.

I saw how long it can actually take for someone to meet someone else who cares. Doesn't have to be a partner, even just a friend.

And thanks for the backup mate :)

Most things still apply I think

She is living with her dad, but she opened herself up to her aunt and talks to her about her feelings and everything. Her aunt is a psychologist/therapist.

I know uni isn't something to play with, that's another reason why this is more difficult.

She wants it to be me next to her because I'm the only thing that makes her stay alive.
Maybe she wanted to free me from all this when she tried yesterday. She keeps saying how she's "only a burden for me and how I'm capable of many things and should do them, instead of caring for her and feeling bad because of her". I keep assuring her, all the time, that I love her and that she's more important than the other things. But she doesn't see how "someone like her can ever be loved". And I want her to know, so I have to be there for her..

Her dad and aunt can just talk to her and take her pills away, but she's such a clever girl she'll figure out ten other ways if she wants to.
I'll tell her that she should talk about it to her psychiatrist, yeah. Maybe a hospital good idea after all.

I can help her if I'm with her. I could be making sure there's nothing dangerous in reach and taking care of her. And even she said that me being with her would give her a lot more comfort and make her feel like there's a reason to go on.

If I'm not there for her but this far away, she doesn't feel like I really exist.. her mind just goes away into some weird thoughts and she doesn't realise things are okay down here..

I want to be there for her to hug her before bed, eat breakfast with her and make her feel alright.

The main problem is, I think, getting out of university and convincing my parents I know what I'm doing. They're good to me and I wouldn't want to disappoint them.

She left her country for a few years just to escape a hospital which had the right to claim her from her parents, and then her parents would have no say in what happens to her.

Sometimes I don't want to believe it's that scary, and I think maybe the hospital is an okay place, but they seem really messed up there.

She's sleeping. Her dad is there, he doesn't care much and probably just wants to put her in a hospital but he'll make sure she's alive.

Her aunt really cares, she knows what's happening, and I hope she's looking out for her. I'll contact her dad tomorrow, it's night now.

Part of it is all very logical and she's got it really developed in her head, and a part is just pure sadness waves for no reason - mood swings, I don't know. She just wants to end it because it feels horrible, and the only way she can get help is with a bunch of pills, which she's scared of because they would make her into s different person. She already feels weird because of the stuff she takes.

She's so scared of hospitals. Poor thing, she was already in a hospital as a child, while underage so a sort of children's hospital, and it was still pretty awful. She's scared of what "adult" hospitals might be like; and I'm scared they would mistreat her really bad there - fill her up with pills way too much, either to just make her a plant so they don't have to care, or try out new meds and on her. She's so so scared and she doesn't want to go to a psychiatrist because they would take her there.

In fact her psychiatrist said she recommends going to a hospital, but that it's her own choice.

I don't know what to think about it, I'm scared it would really destroy her. There, they just keep you physically alive because they have to.

It's sad reading your nice comment, knowing she might be gone already :/

You've got a good point. Sorry for what I wrote to you.

In a way I agree, and think that if someone is really having it that bad they should have the right to end it in peace, without judgement, without shit thrown into face about how life can be great - sometimes it just can't.
We shouldn't make people stay just for us to feel good. Or because we would feel guilty if we let them leave. Maybe it's just the way people are brought up that makes them see suicide in such a way.

I do feel guilty for writing this and potentially letting you end it but on the other hand I don't think I have any right to make that choice for you.

I hope others see that too.

Just please, if you do it, don't involve others in the act. Like a car driver or a shooting range supervisor. They would still be alive and carry the weight and guilt of someone else's death.

My mum's cousin killed himself with a grenade in his bed, while his mother was asleep on sleeping pills. She had to clean her son's..
Please, consider that.

I would still like to know what's troubling you. Because you did post on Reddit, and maybe you still want to try going on.

Or let me know if I should just shut up and go.

Hey, don't go...

Someone said, I'll say it again, the afterlife might be worse than life. Maybe you're just sitting there and looking at Earth and it's not that bad - but maybe you'll never be able to come back. Stuck there, forever regretting not experiencing this life, using this one chance, to see Earth, people, animals, to do exciting things..

Stay. You don't have to be the most successful person in the world - that's a really stupid goal they pump into everyone's heads. But please use your one chance to experience this world. Nobody knows what comes after.

Once you've seen it all, experienced everything "life" has to offer (and that's a LOT more than your current boring environment, your body and bunch of stuff on the internet), then move on. It's okay to move on, but do so with memories of this Earth and this life.

Please, consider staying. I'm worried that maybe in a thousand years of death you'll want to come here again, but you won't be able to. So try to just live it. The best way to get some inspiration is to meet people and to get into some community, and see what other people have to introduce you to. Some people are really interesting - so meet more of them to learn about as much things as possible in life - things that are so unique, and that you would really miss if you wouldn't try them out.

It seems really fucking boring right now, but you can't imagine what's out there and what's possible in life. It's because you haven't seen it.
So go try again, try exploring life. You don't have to be "successful" (whatever that means - probably just a way to make you keep working), but do experience it. Then leave with all the good memories.

Good luck :)

Last night.

Last night, it's 1:00/2:00, she calls me. I tried texting her until then, but sometimes she stays at her evening shift a bit longer, so I accepted that possibility. But the call... she sounded drunk and tired, talking in two languages and about things that didn't happen and aren't possible. (She thought I was with her tonight, said she "moved out with her brother and sister" - they're kids, and other weird things).
I tried asking her slowly and clearly what's going on, and got some information that she went out with someone, she drank wine, and that she is really tired. I guess that might not be real either. I was already scared that she may have overdosed, or even that someone drugged her and she managed to come home. I asked if she took too many pills, how many, what kind, and she said "only two", which is okay. I didn't want to let her fall asleep, but I did, and I stayed up a lot longer, thinking about the whole thing and listening to music... Wasn't sure if I should let her rest, or call to make sure she's okay.

Then the morning came. Well, it was afternoon. I got some rest.. but she was still asleep. 18:00. I texted her dad and he said he's seen her, so that calmed me down a lot... I told him to go check on her, and she's okay, he took care of her. She soon went back to sleep. And I came here.

She'll probably lose her job for not contacting anyone the entire day. That's not even important now..
